As of 2022, 43.5 million Americans have federal student loans. And during the pandemic, 82% of that group paused their monthly repayments. But, starting September 1, interest resumes, and payments are due beginning in October. ➡️

If you're one of the 43.5 million Americans who have to pay student loans this fall, here are 3 #BetterMoneyHabits tips that can help you tackle your student debt even faster.

TIP 1️⃣: Build monthly student loan payments back into your budget. Cutting out any unnecessary expenses can help make it a little easier to digest. (If you’re able, consider paying more than the minimum to help reduce interest over the life of the loan.)

TIP 2️⃣: Understand exactly how much you owe. Having a full view of your financial obligations will help you prioritize and figure out the best payment strategy. (A general rule of thumb is to pay off your highest interest debt first.

TIP 3️⃣: Consolidate your debts into a single, low-interest loan. In addition to your student loans, you could also add in balances from credit cards and other high-interest loans to help you save money and pay debt even faster.
